clue.text: Marine invertebrate crab craftily hid around different pool mostly

indicators.note: done craftily, the letters of crab are cunningly rearranged
around says the word hid wraps itself about the next piece
different says the shortened pool is made into a new order
mostly says the word pool loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A crab slyly conceals something near a pool on the shore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'craftily' and 'different' are both anagram signals, one per piece, and 'mostly' means all but the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Lamp shells are a phylum of shelled sea creatures, invertebrates living on the seabed.

clue.text: A lovable rogue, primarily

indicators.note: rogue, as an adjective meaning wayward, says the letters of the phrase go astray

explanation.surface: Someone describes a charming scoundrel as being, first and foremost, a lovable rogue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rogue' looks like the noun the phrase describes, but it is the anagram signal working on A LOVABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean first and most importantly, an adverbial synonym used to stress the chief point.

clue.text: Game girl but no model, ultimately

indicators.note: but no says the following letter is to be dropped from the girl's name
ultimately says the letter dropped is the final one of the name

parts.note: Bridget is a girl's name
the Model T was the famous Ford car, so model gives T

explanation.surface: A girl turns out to be game, though she is no fashion model in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but no model, ultimately' removes the T (Model T Ford) from the end of BRIDGET.
explanation.definitionFit: Bridge is a card game for four players in two partnerships.

clue.text: Chap getting last letter from Mrs Brown

indicators.note: last letter from says only the final letter of the abbreviation Mrs is used

parts.note: tan is a shade of brown

explanation.surface: A man receives the latest letter from a woman called Mrs Brown.
explanation.definitionFit: Stan is a man's name, and in crosswords any male name can stand for a chap.

clue.text: Teased about large bottom at first — it's wet and messy

indicators.note: at first says the word for bottom is placed at the front

parts.note: a bed is the bottom of a river or sea

indicators.note: about says the word for teased goes round the abbreviation for large

parts.note: ragged, as a past tense, means teased or mocked

explanation.surface: Someone was mocked about their large backside; the result is soggy and untidy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottom' suggests a backside but means a riverbed; 'Teased' is RAGGED as in ragging someone, a British word for mocking.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedraggled describes something made limp and dirty by rain or mud, so wet and messy is a fair paraphrase.

clue.text: Doesn't drink with sailor, as isn't at sea

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters of the phrase are jumbled

explanation.surface: A teetotaller explains that, with a sailor about, he stays dry since he isn't on a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' looks like part of the sailor story but is the anagram signal; the apostrophe in isn't is ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: To abstain is to refrain from alcohol, so the verb matches not drinking.

clue.text: Wordplay comes across flipping poorly? Do this to make things tighter

definitions.text: Do this to make things tighter

indicators.note: comes across says the word for wordplay spans the other piece, holding it inside

parts.note: a pun is a play on words

indicators.note: flipping says the word for poorly is turned back to front

parts.note: poorly means unwell, ill

explanation.surface: A joke falls flat, and advice follows on how to tighten something up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' reads like a mild oath on the surface but signals the reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw in or tighten, as with a belt or reins, is the phrasal verb meant by the instruction.

clue.text: Darned newsreels!

indicators.note: reels means staggers about, so the preceding letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: An exasperated cry against wretched cinema newsreels.
explanation.walkthrough: The one word 'newsreels' splits into NEWS, rearranged, and 'reels', the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Darned fabric is mended by stitching, so it has been stitched.

clue.text: One who dresses edgy characters in theatre, including butcher playing Spiderman?

parts.note: a rober is one who robes, or dresses, someone

indicators.note: including says those edge letters hold the next piece between them
edgy characters are the letters at the edges of the word theatre
playing says the letters of butcher are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A theatrical dresser handles a butcher who is cast as Spiderman.
explanation.walkthrough: Legend says the defeated king, hiding in a cave, watched a spider keep trying to spin its web and took heart: hence 'Spiderman?'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scottish king was famously inspired by watching a persistent spider, making him a spider man.

clue.text: See 9
Warning by daughter before home collapsed

parts.note: cave, Latin for beware, is a schoolboy warning
in means at home

explanation.surface: A daughter gave warning before the house fell down.
explanation.walkthrough: CAVE, pronounced KAY-vee, was a British schoolboy's cry of 'look out'.
explanation.definitionFit: A roof that caved in has fallen inwards, so the phrasal verb means collapsed.

clue.text: Ulster's top spot? Hint: Northern Ireland's ale's brewed but not seen drunk here

indicators.note: brewed says the pool of letters is stirred up into a new order
but not says some letters are taken away from that pool
drunk says the letters to be removed may come in any order

explanation.surface: A tip-off says Northern Irish beer is made but never seen consumed at Ulster's best spot.
explanation.walkthrough: HINT, N and IRELANDS ALES are mixed ('brewed'), with the letters of SEEN ('drunk') taken out ('but not').
explanation.definitionFit: This is the northernmost inhabited island of Northern Ireland, lying off the Antrim coast, so the top spot in Ulster.

clue.text: Silly way battle ends

parts.note: the way a word ends can be described as in a certain letter: in an

indicators.note: ends says the final letter of battle is taken

explanation.surface: A pointless account of how a fight is brought to a close.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as the way 'battle' ends: in an E.
explanation.definitionFit: Inane means senseless or foolish, a direct synonym of silly.

clue.text: ASLEF missing point, going off bad weather warning

indicators.note: going off suggests something spoiled, so the letters are scrambled
missing says the compass point is removed from the union name

parts.note: E, east, is a compass point

explanation.surface: Train drivers' union aims for a strike without reason, warning of storms.
explanation.walkthrough: ASLEF is the British train drivers' union; 'missing' drops E to leave ASLF, and 'off' rearranges that with GOING.
explanation.definitionFit: A foghorn or detonator on railway lines warns of poor visibility, a warning for bad weather.

clue.text: Expedite nothing at all at silly sounding gallery

parts.note: FA is short for sweet Fanny Adams, nothing at all

indicators.note: sounding says the next letters are spelt as the word silly is pronounced

parts.note: the word silly said aloud
the Tate is a London art gallery

explanation.surface: Someone tries to hurry things along at a ridiculous-sounding art gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: Sweet FA is British slang for nothing at all; the Tate is London's best-known gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: To expedite a process is to speed it up or make it easier.

clue.text: Buddhist priest caught having unholy smirk about theory of evolution

parts.note: a lama is a Tibetan Buddhist monk or priest

indicators.note: about says the rearranged letters wrap round the abbreviation for caught
unholy means wicked or disordered, so smirk is rearranged

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A Tibetan monk is caught wearing a wicked grin at a lecture on evolution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unholy' turns SMIRK into RKISM, and 'about' puts it round C.
explanation.definitionFit: Lamarck held that acquired traits are inherited, an early theory of how species develop.

clue.text: Refuge provided by Macau? Silly move after cutback, it appears

indicators.note: after says the rearranged letters follow the earlier pieces

parts.note: split as two words: lop, meaning prune, written backwards

indicators.note: move says the letters of the two words are shifted into a new order

explanation.surface: A puzzled observer suggests that Macau, after budget cuts, made a foolish step in offering shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutback' is one word doing two jobs: LOP (cut) read back. 'move' rearranges MACAU SILLY into ICALASYLUM.
explanation.definitionFit: Political asylum is protection given by a state to a foreign refugee, a form of refuge.

clue.text: One of 13, say, giving support to Harry and his gran

parts.note: a golf tee supports the ball
to harry is to nag
Prince Harry's grandmother was Queen Elizabeth II, Elizabeth Regina, ER

explanation.surface: Someone props up young Prince Harry and his grandmother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harry' looks like the prince but is the verb; 'his gran' then turns the prince back on, giving ER.
explanation.definitionFit: Thirteen is the first of the ages ending in -teen, so a thirteen-year-old is an example.

clue.text: Beware second hands on watch?

parts.note: look out is a call meaning beware

explanation.surface: A warning that a clock's second hand is about to move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hands on watch' looks like clock parts but means crew members keeping watch.
explanation.definitionFit: Hands are workers or crew, and those posted on watch are sentries.

clue.text: Talked foolishly of car journey learner driver went on first

parts.note: a drive is a trip by car
L is the plate for a learner driver
led means went in front, first

explanation.surface: Someone babbles about a car trip on which a learner went ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: To drivel is to talk nonsense, so the past tense matches talked foolishly.

clue.text: See 12
One trying to gain love of woman with alarmed expression

parts.note: ooer is a British exclamation of alarm or surprise

explanation.surface: A suitor's attentions draw a startled cry from a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A suitor courts someone hoping to win affection.

clue.text: Cold and cheerless? If no success at first, just try …

indicators.note: at first says the word for success is placed before the other piece

parts.note: a win is a success

explanation.surface: The old motto: if you fail at first, keep trying, continuing into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Wintry weather is cold, and figuratively a wintry look is bleak and joyless.

clue.text: Braveheart not heartless following impudence? That's noble

indicators.note: following says the final pieces come after the word for impudence

parts.note: gall is cheek or impudence
the heart, or middle letter, of the word brave

indicators.note: heartless says the middle letter of not is removed

explanation.surface: The film hero follows insolence with bravery, and is called noble for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Braveheart' is the film title but reads as the heart of BRAVE, its middle letter; 'heartless' takes the O out of NOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Gallant means chivalrous and honourable, a close synonym of noble in character.

clue.text: … try, try again — to be hot to trot?

parts.note: to have a go is to have a try
again, a go is a try

explanation.surface: The motto concludes, try again, then asks whether that means being eager.
explanation.definitionFit: Go-go describes someone dynamic and keen, eager for action.

clue.text: Scottish victory — poet cut cake first

indicators.note: first says the cake goes ahead of the shortened poet

parts.note: a bannock is a flat Scottish oatcake

indicators.note: cut says the poet's name is trimmed of its final letter

parts.note: Robert Burns is Scotland's national poet

explanation.surface: The Scottish poet ate cake before celebrating a victory.
explanation.definitionFit: Bannockburn, 1314, was Robert the Bruce's decisive victory over the English.

clue.text: See 23 across
Spirit of type in egg flips

indicators.note: flips says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A sort of spirit inside an egg turns over.
explanation.definitionFit: A genie is a magical spirit of Arabian folklore.

clue.text: Salt a setter confused with all but initially Epsom salts

parts.note: a salt is an old sailor, a tar

indicators.note: confused says the remaining letters are jumbled
all but says one letter is dropped from a setter
initially says the first letter of Epsom is the one taken

explanation.surface: A puzzled compiler mixes up chemicals, including Epsom salts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Salt' looks like chemistry but means a sailor; dropping E from A SETTER leaves ASTTER, which 'confused' turns into TRATES.
explanation.definitionFit: Tartrates are compounds of tartaric acid, chemical salts such as cream of tartar.
